title: Design a payments (charges) API
brief: Design the public REST API that merchants use to charge their customers cards. Merchants create a payment, possibly requiring 3-D Secure, then capture it immediately or later. Developer experience and correctness under retries matter most.
constraints: Merchants call from servers with secret keys; browsers use publishable keys only for tokenization
Amounts in minor units with ISO currency
Auth-then-capture and immediate capture
Async steps (3DS) must be representable
Network retries must never double charge

sections.title: Resources & data model
sections.prompt: Model the resources and their states.
keyPoints: PaymentIntent: id (pi_...), amount (integer minor units), currency, status, customer, payment_method, capture_method
Status machine: requires_payment_method -> requires_confirmation -> requires_action -> processing -> requires_capture -> succeeded | canceled
PaymentMethod (pm_...) tokenized card; raw PAN never hits merchant servers
Charge as the underlying attempt record linked to the PaymentIntent
metadata map for merchant key/values; created timestamp; livemode flag

sections.title: Endpoints & methods
keyPoints: POST /v1/payment_intents (create)
GET /v1/payment_intents/{id}; POST /v1/payment_intents/{id} (update)
POST /v1/payment_intents/{id}/confirm, /capture, /cancel as action sub-resources
GET /v1/payment_intents?customer=cus_..&limit=..
Webhook events payment_intent.succeeded / payment_intent.payment_failed for async outcomes

sections.title: Requests, responses & errors
sections.prompt: Show request/response bodies and error handling.
keyPoints: Body: amount=2000&currency=usd&payment_method=pm_..&confirm=true
200 with the full object; 402 for card_declined with decline_code
Error object: {error:{type, code, message, param, decline_code, doc_url}}
400 invalid_request_error with param pointing at the bad field; 401 bad key; 409 idempotency conflict
status requires_action returns next_action {type: redirect_to_url | use_stripe_sdk}

sections.title: Pagination, filtering & idempotency
keyPoints: Idempotency-Key header on all POSTs; key stored with request hash and response for 24h
Same key with a different body -> idempotency_error; concurrent in-flight duplicate -> 409
Cursor pagination: limit (1-100), starting_after / ending_before, has_more
Filter by created[gte]/created[lte], customer
expand[]=customer&expand[]=latest_charge to inline related objects

sections.title: Versioning & evolution
keyPoints: Dated versions (e.g. 2024-06-20) pinned per account; override per request with a version header
Additive changes (new fields, enum values, endpoints) are non-breaking
Clients must tolerate unknown fields and enum values
Breaking changes ship behind a new version with server-side compatibility transforms
Webhooks rendered in the account or endpoint pinned version

sections.title: Auth, limits & safety
keyPoints: Secret key via HTTP Basic/Bearer over TLS only; restricted keys with scopes
Publishable key only for client-side tokenization (reduces PCI scope)
Rate limits with 429 and Retry-After; separate test vs live limits
Validate amount, currency minimums; fraud screening before authorization
Audit log of key usage; test mode isolation via livemode

modelSummary: The API centres on a PaymentIntent resource with an explicit state machine, created via POST /v1/payment_intents and driven by action endpoints /confirm, /capture and /cancel. Amounts are integers in minor units with ISO currency, and raw card data is tokenized client-side into PaymentMethods. Every POST accepts an Idempotency-Key so retries replay the stored response instead of charging twice. Errors use a consistent object with type, code, param and decline_code, and async steps surface via next_action plus webhooks. Lists use cursor pagination with starting_after and has_more, and expand[] inlines related objects. Evolution uses dated, account-pinned versions with additive changes by default. Endpoints: POST /v1/payment_intents, GET /v1/payment_intents/{id}, POST /v1/payment_intents/{id}, POST /v1/payment_intents/{id}/confirm, POST /v1/payment_intents/{id}/capture, POST /v1/payment_intents/{id}/cancel, GET /v1/payment_intents.

title: Design a refunds API
brief: Design the API that lets merchants refund all or part of a successful payment. Refunds can take days to settle and may fail. Ensure merchants cannot over-refund and can safely retry.
constraints: Full and multiple partial refunds per payment
Total refunded must never exceed the captured amount
Refunds are async: pending -> succeeded | failed
Reasons: duplicate, fraudulent, requested_by_customer
Merchants reconcile via webhooks and list endpoints

sections.title: Resources & data model
keyPoints: Refund: id (re_...), payment_intent/charge, amount, currency, status, reason, failure_reason, metadata, created
Status: pending, requires_action, succeeded, failed, canceled
Charge exposes amount_refunded, refunded boolean and a refunds list
Balance transaction records the money movement for reconciliation
Currency always equals the original charge currency

sections.title: Endpoints & methods
keyPoints: POST /v1/refunds {payment_intent, amount?, reason?}
GET /v1/refunds/{id}; POST /v1/refunds/{id} (update metadata only)
POST /v1/refunds/{id}/cancel (only while pending and supported by the method)
GET /v1/refunds?payment_intent=pi_..
Events: refund.created, refund.updated, charge.refunded

sections.title: Requests, responses & errors
keyPoints: Omitted amount means refund the remaining refundable amount
200 returns the Refund with status pending or succeeded
400 amount_too_large when amount > captured - already refunded
400 charge_already_refunded; 400 charge_disputed when a dispute exists
Failed refunds surface failure_reason (e.g. expired_or_canceled_card) via refund.updated webhook

sections.title: Pagination, filtering & idempotency
keyPoints: Idempotency-Key is essential: a retried partial refund must not refund twice
Server enforces refundable balance under a row lock on the charge (atomic check-and-insert)
Cursor pagination with starting_after, limit, has_more
Filter by payment_intent, charge, created range
expand[]=charge for reconciliation

sections.title: Versioning & evolution
keyPoints: New reason or status values are additive; clients must handle unknown enums
Moving from charge-centric to payment_intent-centric refunds via a new dated version
Deprecated fields stay populated on old versions
Webhook payloads serialized in the endpoint pinned version
State machine changes documented in the changelog

sections.title: Auth, limits & safety
keyPoints: Refunds require a secret key with write scope; restricted keys can exclude refunds
Rate limits and anomaly alerts on refund bursts (compromised key)
Audit trail of who issued each refund (dashboard user vs API key)
Funds only return to the original payment method
Webhook signatures so merchants can trust refund events

modelSummary: Refunds are a first-class resource created with POST /v1/refunds referencing a payment_intent, with an optional amount for partial refunds and a reason enum. The server atomically checks refundable balance (captured minus already refunded) under a lock, returning 400 amount_too_large on overdraw, and Idempotency-Key ensures retries do not double refund. Refunds are asynchronous with statuses pending, succeeded, failed and canceled, reported through refund.updated and charge.refunded webhooks. Lists support cursor pagination and filtering by payment_intent. New statuses and reasons are additive under dated versions. Endpoints: POST /v1/refunds, GET /v1/refunds/{id}, POST /v1/refunds/{id}, POST /v1/refunds/{id}/cancel, GET /v1/refunds.

title: Design a subscriptions API
brief: Design the API for recurring billing: merchants define products and prices, subscribe customers, change plans mid-cycle with proration, and handle failed renewals. The API must make the billing lifecycle explicit.
constraints: Monthly/yearly prices, per-seat quantity
Trials, upgrades/downgrades with proration
Invoices generated per cycle and charged automatically
Failed payments retried (dunning) before cancel
Cancel immediately or at period end

sections.title: Resources & data model
keyPoints: Product and Price (unit_amount, currency, recurring {interval, interval_count}); prices immutable once used
Customer with a default payment method
Subscription: customer, items[] (price, quantity), status, current_period_start/end, trial_end, cancel_at_period_end
Status: incomplete, trialing, active, past_due, unpaid, canceled
Invoice and InvoiceLineItem per cycle, paid via a PaymentIntent

sections.title: Endpoints & methods
keyPoints: POST /v1/products, POST /v1/prices, POST /v1/customers
POST /v1/subscriptions {customer, items:[{price, quantity}], trial_period_days}
POST /v1/subscriptions/{id} to change items/quantity with proration_behavior
DELETE /v1/subscriptions/{id} (cancel now) vs POST with cancel_at_period_end=true
GET /v1/invoices/upcoming?subscription=.. to preview proration

sections.title: Requests, responses & errors
keyPoints: If the first payment needs SCA, status is incomplete with latest_invoice.payment_intent.next_action
proration_behavior: create_prorations | none | always_invoice
400 resource_missing for unknown price; 400 on currency mismatch with existing subscriptions
402 when an immediate invoice payment fails with a card error
Webhooks: invoice.paid, invoice.payment_failed, customer.subscription.updated / deleted

sections.title: Pagination, filtering & idempotency
keyPoints: GET /v1/subscriptions?customer=&status=&price= with cursor pagination
Idempotency-Key on create and update to avoid duplicate subscriptions
expand[]=latest_invoice.payment_intent saves round trips
expand[]=data.items.data.price on lists avoids N+1 calls
Upcoming invoice is a side-effect-free GET preview

sections.title: Versioning & evolution
keyPoints: Prices are immutable: change pricing by creating a new Price and migrating subscriptions
New statuses (e.g. paused) are additive but must be documented as possible values
Plans -> Prices migration handled via a dated version with a compatibility layer
Default proration behavior only changes in a new version
Event payloads rendered in the endpoint pinned version

sections.title: Auth, limits & safety
keyPoints: Secret key auth; customer portal uses short-lived scoped session links
Rate limits per account; bulk migrations through async batch jobs
Billing anchored in UTC with billing_cycle_anchor
Configurable dunning schedule with a bounded number of retries
Test clocks to simulate time advancing in test mode

modelSummary: The billing API models immutable Prices under Products, Customers with default payment methods, and Subscriptions made of items (price, quantity) with an explicit status machine (incomplete, trialing, active, past_due, unpaid, canceled). Each cycle produces an Invoice charged via a PaymentIntent, and failed payments follow a configurable dunning schedule announced by invoice.payment_failed webhooks. Plan changes go through POST /v1/subscriptions/{id} with proration_behavior, and GET /v1/invoices/upcoming previews the result. Cancellation is immediate via DELETE or deferred via cancel_at_period_end. Creates are idempotent and lists use cursors and expand. Endpoints: POST /v1/products, POST /v1/prices, POST /v1/customers, POST /v1/subscriptions, GET /v1/subscriptions/{id}, POST /v1/subscriptions/{id}, DELETE /v1/subscriptions/{id}, GET /v1/invoices/upcoming.

title: Design a webhooks endpoint management API
brief: Merchants want to receive events (payment succeeded, refund failed) at their own HTTPS URLs. Design the API to register and manage webhook endpoints plus the delivery contract: payload shape, signing, retries and replay.
constraints: Each account may have up to 16 endpoints
Endpoints subscribe to specific event types or *
At-least-once delivery with retries for up to 3 days
Payloads must be verifiable by the receiver
Merchants need to inspect and resend past events

sections.title: Resources & data model
keyPoints: WebhookEndpoint: id (we_...), url, enabled_events[], status (enabled/disabled), api_version, secret (returned once), description
Event: id (evt_...), type, created, data.object snapshot, data.previous_attributes, api_version
DeliveryAttempt: endpoint, event, http status, latency, next_retry_at
Events immutable and retained for 30 days
Secret rotation keeps multiple active secrets during an overlap window

sections.title: Endpoints & methods
keyPoints: POST /v1/webhook_endpoints {url, enabled_events}
GET / POST / DELETE /v1/webhook_endpoints/{id}
GET /v1/events?type=payment_intent.succeeded&created[gte]=..
GET /v1/events/{id}; POST /v1/webhook_endpoints/{id}/events/{evt_id}/resend
POST /v1/webhook_endpoints/{id}/rotate_secret

sections.title: Requests, responses & errors
keyPoints: Delivery: POST Event JSON with header Stripe-Signature: t=timestamp,v1=hex(HMAC_SHA256(secret, t + "." + raw_body))
Receiver returns 2xx quickly; non-2xx or timeout (~10s) counts as failure
Exponential backoff retries; endpoint disabled after sustained failure and owner emailed
400 url_invalid for non-HTTPS or private IP; 400 for unknown event type
Receivers dedupe on event.id because delivery is at-least-once and unordered

sections.title: Pagination, filtering & idempotency
keyPoints: Events list uses cursor pagination (starting_after, has_more), newest first
No ordering guarantee; receivers re-fetch the object if order matters
Idempotency-Key on endpoint creation to avoid duplicate registrations
Filter events by type, created range, delivery_success=false
Thin events option: send ids only and let receivers fetch current state

sections.title: Versioning & evolution
keyPoints: Endpoint pinned to api_version; payloads rendered in that version
New event types are additive and delivered only if subscribed or *
Upgrading an endpoint version is explicit; run a second endpoint in parallel to migrate
Add a v2 signature alongside v1 rather than replacing silently
Deprecate event types with long notice

sections.title: Auth, limits & safety
keyPoints: Verify HMAC with constant-time compare and reject timestamps older than 5 minutes (replay protection)
SSRF protection: HTTPS only, block private/link-local IPs, resolve DNS at send time
Secrets shown once at creation and rotatable with overlap
Per-endpoint concurrency caps so receivers are not overwhelmed
Publish source IP ranges for optional allowlisting

modelSummary: WebhookEndpoint resources (url, enabled_events, api_version, secret) are managed via CRUD under /v1/webhook_endpoints, and Events are immutable records listable via GET /v1/events. Delivery POSTs the Event JSON with a Stripe-Signature header containing a timestamp and HMAC-SHA256 over timestamp.raw_body; receivers verify with constant-time comparison and a 5 minute tolerance. Delivery is at-least-once and unordered, retried with exponential backoff for up to 3 days before the endpoint is disabled, so receivers dedupe on event.id. Secrets rotate with an overlap window, URLs are validated against SSRF, and payloads render in the endpoint pinned version. Endpoints: POST /v1/webhook_endpoints, GET /v1/webhook_endpoints, GET /v1/webhook_endpoints/{id}, POST /v1/webhook_endpoints/{id}, DELETE /v1/webhook_endpoints/{id}, POST /v1/webhook_endpoints/{id}/rotate_secret, GET /v1/events, GET /v1/events/{id}.

title: Design pagination for a list endpoint
brief: Our GET /v1/transactions endpoint returns millions of rows for large merchants, and offset pagination is timing out and returning duplicates. Redesign pagination, filtering and sorting for this list endpoint.
constraints: Up to hundreds of millions of rows per account
New rows inserted continuously while clients page
Filters: created range, status, customer
Default sort newest first
Some clients are scripts exporting everything

sections.title: Resources & data model
keyPoints: List envelope: {object:"list", data:[...], has_more, url}
Transactions have a stable unique id and created timestamp
Sort key (created DESC, id DESC) is unique and stable
total_count omitted by default (expensive); opt-in only
Cursor is the last object id or an opaque token encoding (created, id) plus filter hash

sections.title: Endpoints & methods
keyPoints: GET /v1/transactions?limit=50&starting_after=txn_..
GET /v1/transactions?ending_before=txn_.. for backward paging
GET /v1/transactions/search?query=.. for flexible search with eventually consistent semantics
POST /v1/reporting/exports for bulk async export instead of paging millions
SDK auto-pagination helpers iterate pages transparently

sections.title: Requests, responses & errors
keyPoints: limit default 10, max 100; 400 if out of range
400 if cursor object is not found or belongs to a different filter set
Invalid filter param returns 400 with param set
Empty page returns 200 with data:[] and has_more:false
Opaque keyset cursors stay valid even if the referenced row is deleted

sections.title: Pagination, filtering & idempotency
sections.prompt: Explain why cursor beats offset and how filtering combines.
keyPoints: Offset scans and discards skipped rows (O(offset)) and shifts on inserts, causing duplicates/skips
Keyset: WHERE (created, id) < (:c, :id) ORDER BY created DESC, id DESC LIMIT n+1; extra row sets has_more
Composite index (account_id, created DESC, id DESC) plus filter-specific indexes
created[gte]/created[lt] bound the scan; status filter via composite or partial index
GETs are safe and idempotent, so no Idempotency-Key is needed

sections.title: Versioning & evolution
keyPoints: Offset kept on the old version, cursor on the new dated version
Adding filters is additive; changing default sort order is breaking
Opaque cursor format lets internals change freely
Raising max limit is safe; lowering it is breaking
Document consistency semantics (live view, not snapshot)

sections.title: Auth, limits & safety
keyPoints: Every query scoped by authenticated account (tenant id)
Rate limits per request; large exports pushed to async jobs
Signed/encrypted cursors prevent tampering and cross-account use
Optional cursor expiry
Avoid count(*) on huge tables; return has_more instead

modelSummary: The endpoint moves from offset to keyset (cursor) pagination: results sort by a unique, stable (created DESC, id DESC) key and the cursor identifies the last row, so each page is an index range scan of limit+1 rows regardless of depth, and concurrent inserts do not cause duplicates or skips. Responses use a list envelope with data and has_more; requests accept limit (max 100), starting_after and ending_before plus filters like created[gte] and status. Cursors are opaque, signed, tied to the filter set and tenant-scoped. Totals are omitted by default, and bulk needs go to an async export. Endpoints: GET /v1/transactions, GET /v1/transactions/{id}, GET /v1/transactions/search, POST /v1/reporting/exports, GET /v1/reporting/exports/{id}.

title: Design an API versioning strategy
brief: We have thousands of integrations that cannot all upgrade at once, yet we need to keep improving the API. Design a versioning strategy that lets us ship breaking changes without breaking anyone.
constraints: Integrations live for years without code changes
We ship changes weekly
Webhooks and SDKs must respect versions
Supporting old versions must stay cheap
Clear developer upgrade path

sections.title: Resources & data model
sections.prompt: What is versioned and how is it represented?
keyPoints: Dated versions (e.g. 2024-06-20) rather than v1/v2 major paths
Account gets a pinned default version at its first request
Each version is a set of named change modules
Per-request override via Stripe-Version header
Webhook endpoints carry their own pinned api_version

sections.title: Endpoints & methods
keyPoints: Path stays /v1/...; version travels in a header, not the URL
Account settings show the pinned version; dashboard upgrade action
Developers test an upgrade per request with the header before switching
Changelog per version with migration notes
A /v2 namespace reserved for wholesale redesigns only

sections.title: Requests, responses & errors
sections.prompt: How do requests flow through versions?
keyPoints: Core code implements only the latest version
Responses pass through transforms walking backwards from latest to the requested version
Request params are transformed forward to latest
Unknown version header -> 400 listing valid versions
Response echoes the version used

sections.title: Pagination, filtering & idempotency
sections.prompt: How do lists and idempotency interact with versions?
keyPoints: Idempotent replays return the response rendered in the original request version
Pagination cursors remain valid across versions
Expanded objects transformed the same way as top-level objects
Events stored version-neutral and rendered per endpoint version
Golden-response contract tests per version

sections.title: Versioning & evolution
keyPoints: Non-breaking: new endpoints, optional params, new response fields, new event types
Breaking: removing/renaming fields, changing types, new required params, changing defaults or error codes
New enum values documented as non-breaking; clients must handle unknowns
Deprecation via Deprecation and Sunset headers plus dashboard notices
Retire a transform only when usage telemetry reaches zero

sections.title: Auth, limits & safety
keyPoints: Track version usage per account to plan deprecations
Allow rollback to the previous version within a window after upgrade
SDKs pin the version matching their generated types
Auth and rate limits independent of version
Fuzz/contract tests ensure old versions never change

modelSummary: Use dated API versions pinned per account at first use, overridable per request with a Stripe-Version header, while the URL stays /v1. Core logic implements only the latest version; a chain of small version change modules transforms requests forward and responses backward to the caller version, so each old version costs only a transform. Additive changes (new fields, endpoints, optional params) ship without a new version; removals, renames, type and default changes require one. Webhooks and idempotent replays render in the pinned version, and usage telemetry plus Deprecation/Sunset headers guide retirement. Endpoints: any /v1/* with optional Stripe-Version header, GET /v1/account (shows pinned version), POST /v1/account/api_version (upgrade, or via dashboard), and a public upgrades changelog.

title: Design idempotent POST requests
brief: Clients retry POST requests on timeouts and network errors, and we have seen double charges. Design an idempotency mechanism for all mutating endpoints of a payments API, including what is stored, for how long, and how concurrent duplicates behave.
constraints: Any POST may be retried by clients or SDKs automatically
Requests may involve external calls (card networks)
Keys provided by clients, retained 24 hours
Distributed API servers behind a load balancer
Must be safe even if the server crashes mid-request

sections.title: Resources & data model
keyPoints: IdempotencyRecord: unique (account_id, key), request_hash, status (in_progress/completed), response_code, response_body, recovery_point, locked_at, created_at
Keys scoped per account and per mode (test/live)
request_hash = method + path + normalized body
Records expire after 24h
Recovery points for multi-step operations (atomic phases)

sections.title: Endpoints & methods
keyPoints: Idempotency-Key header accepted on all POST endpoints
GET and DELETE are idempotent by HTTP semantics and ignore the header
SDKs auto-generate a UUIDv4 per logical request and reuse it on retries
Response header Idempotent-Replayed: true on replay
Keys are opaque; no management endpoints

sections.title: Requests, responses & errors
keyPoints: First request: insert record in_progress atomically (unique constraint), then execute
Retry after completion: replay stored status and body verbatim, including 4xx
Retry while in progress: 409 Conflict; client retries later
Same key with different parameters: 400 idempotency_error
Server crash: lock expires and a retry resumes from recovery_point

sections.title: Pagination, filtering & idempotency
keyPoints: Pass an idempotency key downstream to the card processor so external calls dedupe too
Split work into atomic phases each committed with a recovery point
Transactional outbox emits events/webhooks exactly once from the DB
Do not persist transient 5xx results; allow the retry to execute
Clients use exponential backoff with jitter

sections.title: Versioning & evolution
keyPoints: Replays render in the original request API version
Changing body normalization must not reject legitimate retries
Lengthening retention is safe; shortening is breaking
Document which endpoints honour keys
Extend to batch endpoints with per-item keys

sections.title: Auth, limits & safety
keyPoints: Keys scoped per account so one tenant cannot read another tenant cached response
Limit key length (e.g. 255 chars)
Replays count against rate limits to prevent abuse
Stored responses may hold sensitive data: encrypt at rest, delete on TTL
Monitor 409/400 idempotency errors as a signal of client bugs

modelSummary: Every POST accepts an Idempotency-Key header; the server atomically inserts an IdempotencyRecord keyed by (account, key) with a request hash and status in_progress before doing any work. Completed requests store the status code and body so retries replay the exact response with Idempotent-Replayed: true, mismatched parameters return an idempotency error, and concurrent duplicates get 409. Multi-step operations commit atomic phases with recovery points, pass keys downstream to processors and emit events through a transactional outbox, so crashes resume safely. Records are tenant-scoped, encrypted and expire after 24 hours; SDKs generate UUIDv4 keys and retry with backoff. Endpoints: POST /v1/payment_intents, POST /v1/refunds, POST /v1/customers (all honouring Idempotency-Key), with response headers Idempotent-Replayed and Request-Id.

title: Design a file upload API
brief: Merchants need to upload documents (dispute evidence, identity documents) up to 50 MB, and some will upload over unreliable connections. Design the upload API, file references and how files attach to other resources.
constraints: Files up to 50 MB; allowed types PDF, JPEG, PNG
Purpose determines allowed types and access
Resumable uploads for flaky clients
Files referenced by other objects (disputes, verifications)
Downloads via expiring links

sections.title: Resources & data model
keyPoints: File: id (file_...), purpose, filename, size (bytes), type, status, created, expires_at
FileLink: id, file, url, expires_at for temporary sharing
UploadSession for resumable uploads: id, size, received_bytes, parts
Purposes: dispute_evidence, identity_document, business_logo
Bytes in object storage; metadata in the database

sections.title: Endpoints & methods
keyPoints: POST /v1/files (multipart/form-data: file, purpose) on a dedicated upload host
GET /v1/files/{id}; GET /v1/files?purpose=..
GET /v1/files/{id}/contents or via a FileLink url
Resumable: POST /v1/upload_sessions -> PUT /v1/upload_sessions/{id} with Content-Range -> POST /v1/upload_sessions/{id}/complete
POST /v1/file_links {file, expires_at}; attach via POST /v1/disputes/{id} evidence[receipt]=file_...

sections.title: Requests, responses & errors
keyPoints: 200 returns File object with status uploaded or processing (scan pending)
413 Payload Too Large over the limit; 415 Unsupported Media Type for the purpose
400 invalid purpose; 404 unknown upload session
Resumable PUT reports received range; client resumes from the last byte
Checksum (SHA-256) verified; mismatch -> 400

sections.title: Pagination, filtering & idempotency
keyPoints: Cursor pagination on GET /v1/files
Idempotency-Key on file creation so retried uploads do not duplicate
Parts idempotent by part number/offset
Filter by purpose and created range
File unusable until virus scan passes

sections.title: Versioning & evolution
keyPoints: New purposes and types are additive
Presigned direct-to-storage uploads offered as a new flow alongside the old
File fields additive; size always in bytes
Legacy endpoints deprecated with Sunset headers
Content URLs stable across API versions

sections.title: Auth, limits & safety
keyPoints: Validate type by magic bytes, not extension; malware scan
Encrypt at rest; identity documents restricted to owner and never exposed via FileLinks
FileLinks unguessable and expiring; served from a separate domain to avoid XSS
Per-account upload rate and bandwidth limits
Strip EXIF metadata where appropriate

modelSummary: Files are first-class resources uploaded via multipart POST to a dedicated upload host with a required purpose that governs allowed types, size limits and access. Large or flaky uploads use an UploadSession with ranged PUTs, checksums and a complete call, and file creation honours Idempotency-Key. File objects (id, purpose, size, type, status) are referenced by id from other resources like dispute evidence, and downloads go through expiring FileLinks served from a separate domain. Validation errors use 413, 415 and 400 with the standard error object, and content is type-sniffed, malware scanned and encrypted at rest. Endpoints: POST /v1/files, GET /v1/files, GET /v1/files/{id}, GET /v1/files/{id}/contents, POST /v1/upload_sessions, PUT /v1/upload_sessions/{id}, POST /v1/upload_sessions/{id}/complete, POST /v1/file_links.

title: Design an API error model
brief: Our API returns errors inconsistently: some are strings, some HTML, some 200s with error fields. Design a consistent error model covering HTTP status codes, a machine-readable error body, and how SDKs and developers should handle each class of error.
constraints: Public REST API used from many languages
Errors must be machine-handleable and human-friendly
Must distinguish retryable from non-retryable
Must support field-level validation errors
Must not leak internal details

sections.title: Resources & data model
keyPoints: {"error":{"type","code","message","param","doc_url","request_id"}}
type: api_error, card_error, idempotency_error, invalid_request_error, authentication_error, rate_limit_error
code: stable machine string (resource_missing, parameter_invalid_integer)
message: human readable and may change; never parse it
Optional details[] for multiple field violations (RFC 9457 problem+json as an alternative)

sections.title: Endpoints & methods
sections.prompt: How do errors appear across endpoints?
keyPoints: Every endpoint uses the same envelope with Content-Type application/json
Request-Id header on all responses for support
Webhook delivery failures surface as delivery attempt records
Batch endpoints return per-item errors only where documented
SDKs map error types to exception classes

sections.title: Requests, responses & errors
keyPoints: 400 invalid request/validation; 401 missing or invalid key; 403 insufficient permission
404 resource_missing; 409 conflict (idempotency in progress, state conflict)
402 request failed, e.g. card declined with decline_code
429 rate limited with Retry-After
500/502/503/504 server-side: retryable with the same Idempotency-Key

sections.title: Pagination, filtering & idempotency
sections.prompt: Retries and idempotency in error handling.
keyPoints: Retryable: 409 lock conflicts, 429, 5xx and network errors; non-retryable: 400/401/402/403/404
Retries must reuse the same Idempotency-Key
Completed idempotent requests replay their original error
Invalid cursor returns 400 with param=starting_after
Exponential backoff with jitter; honour Retry-After

sections.title: Versioning & evolution
keyPoints: Adding new codes is additive; clients default-handle unknown codes by type
Changing a code or status for an existing condition is breaking
Messages can be improved freely because clients must not parse them
doc_url points to stable per-code docs
Remove or rename types only via a new version

sections.title: Auth, limits & safety
keyPoints: Never expose stack traces, SQL or internal hostnames
Return 404 (not 403) for resources in other accounts to avoid existence leaks
Uniform authentication errors to prevent key enumeration
Log full detail internally keyed by request_id
Rate limit headers: X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset

modelSummary: All errors use a single JSON envelope {error:{type, code, message, param, doc_url, request_id}} with the appropriate HTTP status: type is a small fixed set, code a stable machine identifier, param names the offending field, and message is for humans only. Status mapping is explicit: 400 validation, 401 auth, 402 request failed (declines), 403 permission, 404 missing, 409 conflict, 429 rate limited with Retry-After, and 5xx server errors. Clients retry only 409 lock conflicts, 429, 5xx and network errors, reusing the same Idempotency-Key with backoff. New codes are additive; changing an existing code or status is breaking. No internal details leak, cross-tenant resources return 404, and every response carries a Request-Id. Examples: POST /v1/payment_intents -> 402 {error:{type:"card_error", code:"card_declined", decline_code:"insufficient_funds"}}; GET /v1/customers/cus_x -> 404 resource_missing; POST /v1/refunds -> 400 {param:"amount", code:"amount_too_large"}.
